thread:
sam: Heads up — canary for raven-v3q-int8 (onboard) is showing a spike in structured-output validation failures after quantization. baseline was ~0.4% parse errors, canary at 8.3% across funcall endpoints.

maria: Ugh. Are these outright malformed JSONs or extra fields that break strict schema?

sam: Mostly extra/unknown top-level keys (e.g. "debug_trace", "confidence_scores") and occasionally arrays where objects expected. Not typical truncation.

pavan: Any pattern by prompt type? short vs long context?

sam: Preliminary slice shows heavy for prompts that include multi-step toolchains and when KV cache prefixing is used. Also higher when temp >= 0.7.

jess: Do we have telemetry logs of the exact payloads failing validator? Could run an NDJSON export and sample.

sam: Yes — pulled 2k failures into S3: s3://redwood-canary/raven-v3q-int8/failures/2026-03-19.ndjson. Quick SQL on events: 
```
SELECT count(*) as n, failure_kind FROM funcall_validations WHERE model='raven-v3q-int8' GROUP BY failure_kind ORDER BY n DESC LIMIT 10;
```
Top kind = unexpected_field, then array_instead_of_object.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout: raven-v3q-int8 -> 5% traffic in prod region-us-west-2 (2026-03-19T08:42Z)

schema-validator: Observed 167 unexpected_field errors (8.3% of sampled). Validator configured strict=true.

maria: Two options: 1) relax validator to allow unknown keys (soft mode) + warn; 2) add an adaptive postprocess stage that strips unknown keys and normalizes arrays -> object mappings; 3) rollback canary to previous version. Thoughts?

pavan: I vote for (2) short-term while we root cause. We should not silently accept unknown fields without logging — but stripping with telemetry is ok.

jess: Agree, use adaptor approach and run A/B: adaptor-on vs adaptor-off. Measure acceptance rate and golden eval harm. Also capture the stripped keys for analysis.

sam: Prototype adaptor (python pseudo):
```
def schema_adaptor(parsed_json, schema):
    allowed = set(schema['properties'].keys())
    stripped = {k: parsed_json.pop(k) for k in list(parsed_json.keys()) if k not in allowed}
    # convert single-element arrays to scalar objects when schema expects object
    for k, v in list(parsed_json.items()):
        if schema['properties'].get(k, {}).get('type') == 'object' and isinstance(v, list) and len(v)==1:
            parsed_json[k] = v[0]
    return parsed_json, stripped
```
We'll persist stripped as telemetry event.

maria: Also add a deterministic fallback: if adaptor changes structure in a way that differs from golden on a small human-eval set, surface for manual triage.

pavan: We should also instrument the model input side — check if prompt template injection is adding debug fields (unlikely) or if quantization kernel is changing tokenization of tool-call wrapper (more plausible).

sam: Good call. Requesting a quick tokenization diff for a sample that produced "confidence_scores" field. @jess can you run token diff against float and int8 runs?

jess: On it, will produce a tiny report by EOD.

deploy-bot: Canary update: adaptor-enabled -> 2.5% traffic (A/B control still 2.5%)

sam: Quick success metric: reduce schema failures from 8.3% -> <1% and no >1% delta in gold eval BLEU/acceptance on our 500-sample golden set.

maria: Also define retention policy for stripped keys events and add a k-anonymization step before storing free-text in telemetry.

pavan: Action items:
- jess: tokenization diff + sample dump (EOD)
- sam: implement adaptor + telemetry + deploy canary split (today)
- maria: add privacy filter and human-eval protocol for checking adaptor impact (tomorrow)
- jess/pavan: if adaptor fixes >90% but we still see weird arrays, iterate with small postprocess heuristics

jess: thumbs up. I'll also start an eval run comparing raven-v3q-int8 vs raven-v3q-fp16 on the toolcall suite (1k cases) to quantify functional regressions.

schema-validator: Note: toggling strict=false will affect all models. Prefer adaptor path to maintain strictness.

sam: Agreed. Rolling adaptor for canary now, will report back metrics in ~2 hours. :rocket:

maria: If adaptor reduces failures but we find the root cause in tokenization/decoding, prioritize a model-side fix in next release.

pavan: If model-side fix is nontrivial, we should bake the adaptor into the serving runtime as a configurable stage to keep consistent behavior across Dedicated/Private deployments.

sam: Good point — keep it lightweight and config-driven.

jess: update: token diff shows an extra prompt sentinel token sequence sometimes causing the decoder to emit a small diagnostic array under "debug_trace". Seems correlated with kv-prefixing edge-case. More in the report.

sam: thanks. if adaptor can't fully bridge, we'll cut canary and open a ticket for kernel/kv-prefix fix.

maria: :+1: keep the human eval lot small and high-priority to ensure no subtle regressions.

[thread ends — sampler will post follow-up with metrics]
